names.name: heavy tomato sauce
names.said: 'Sweet' or 'mild' on Upstate menus; 'barbecue sauce', without qualification, to most of the country.

text.what: A thick red sauce built on tomato — ketchup, paste or sauce — sweetened with brown sugar or molasses, soured with vinegar and seasoned with spices, cooked down until it clings. It is the sauce of the western and northwestern corner of South Carolina on the state's four-sauce map: the tourism office's 'tomato-and-sugar sauce', the one it says you are most likely to find on a grocery shelf. It goes on after cooking — on the plate, on the bun, on ribs and chicken — and sits on the meat rather than soaking in.
text.story: This is the national sauce at the state's edge. Heinz put out the first major bottled barbecue sauce in 1940, General Foods' Open Pit followed, Kraft came in around 1960 and advertised its way to first place, and after the war the sugar and the ingredient count of sauces climbed; the typical commercial sauce is the Kansas City kind, 'thick, reddish-brown, tomato-based, and made with sugar, vinegar, and spices', which Wikipedia's sauce history places downstream of the Piedmont's thin dip and Memphis's sauce. The South Carolina Barbeque Association says the heavy tomato sauce 'evolved only recently, that is, in the last sixty or so years', pushed by commercial brands, and Wikipedia's South Carolina article calls it 'more similar to sauces popular in other states'. *Inference —* a sauce that arrived by bottle would settle where the older sauces were thinnest on the ground, at the state's western edge, farthest from the whole-hog coast and the German Midlands. Henry's Smokehouse in Greenville makes its own tomato-based mild sauce by hand and sets a mustard-based spicy one beside it.
text.how: Simmer tomato with brown sugar or molasses, vinegar, salt, black pepper and spices until it thickens. It is a finishing and table sauce: brushed on ribs and chicken near the end of cooking or served alongside, spooned over chopped pork on the plate. It is the one Carolina sauce that coats rather than soaks.
text.today: Henry's Smokehouse in Greenville serves its tomato-based mild sauce beside a mustard one; national bottles fill the western shelves. Greenwood's July Festival of Discovery judges Carolina barbecue and hash under Kansas City Barbeque Society rules.

recipes.title: Barbecue Sauce (Kansas City-style)
ingredients: 3 tablespoons (45 mL) finely minced yellow onion
4 teaspoons (20 mL) bottled liquid smoke flavor (hickory)
¼ teaspoon (1 mL) Louisiana-style red pepper sauce
recipes.text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a saucepan.
2. Mix well.
3. Simmer over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
recipes.note: The thick sweet style the up-country South Carolina sauces sit closest to: ketchup, brown sugar, Worcestershire, butter, a little vinegar, liquid smoke.

recipes.title: Barbecue Sauce I
ingredients: 1 heaping tsp (6.66 mL) of ground coffee beans
A shot of whiskey or ½ shot of cognac
recipes.text:
1. Mix everything in a pot.
2. Let it simmer for around 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
recipes.note: Ketchup, brown sugar, paprika, garlic and a heaping teaspoon of ground coffee, simmered half an hour.

recipes.title: Barbecue Sauce (Sweet)
ingredients: Garlic powder or minced garlic to taste (optional)
recipes.text:
1. Combine all ingredients together and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer 10 to 15 minutes, until it thickens slightly.
2. Arrange chicken pieces or pork chops in a greased baking dish.
3. Pour half of sauce over and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30 to 40 minutes.
4. Pour remaining sauce over before serving.

recipes.title: Barbecue Sauce II
recipes.text:
1. Mix everything in a pot.
2. To use, heat the sauce with some pre-cooked meat in it.
recipes.note: Three ingredients: ketchup, molasses, liquid smoke. The shortest way to the thick red end of the range.

ingredients: Vegan Worcestershire Sauce (Water, Distilled Vinegar, Sugar, Salt, Molasses, Caramel Color, Tamarind, Onion and Garlic)
Organic Yellow Mustard (Organic Distilled Vinegar, Organic Mustard Seed, Salt, Organic Turmeric, Organic Spices)
profile.note: Sugar first, tomato second, vinegar fourth: the order runs opposite to the eastern sauce's. Six grams of sugar to the tablespoon, against about 12.6 g in a tablespoon of table sugar. Made in Raleigh, which is eastern North Carolina — the thick sauce is not confined to the state lines its name suggests. Ingredients from the maker's page, revision code 26-1; sugar and sodium from USDA FoodData Central record 1862954, which lists the same ingredients.
